observations.behavior: Documentation update: added a 50-cell notebook limit and failure behavior.
observations.code_quote: "description": "Add a cell to a markdown notebook. SQL and Python cells run immediately: the call waits up to ~45s and returns the result — columns, a capped row preview, stdout/stderr (a Python cell's logs and tracebacks), and error — so you can look at the output and decide the next step (fix, or proceed). If the status comes back 'running', poll notebooks-run-cell-result with the run_id. A cell that reads other cells' dataframes references them by dataframe_name; those cells must have completed a run first, so add cells in dependency order. SQL cells are always HogQL: queries against PostHog or data warehouse tables run on ClickHouse, and a SQL cell that references a Python-created dataframe runs on the notebook's local engine automatically — any local dataframe is queryable by name, same syntax. The first Python cell can take longer while the notebook's sandbox kernel starts. Run analysis Python here rather than in a runtime the user can't see — dataframe work, statistics, clustering, forecasting, plotting — so the code and its output stay visible and re-runnable beside the result; the sandbox has pandas, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, and matplotlib. component cells add other node types: Query, Image, Embed, Latex, FeatureFlag, Survey, Experiment, Person, Cohort, Recording, RecordingPlaylist. Pass a short title on every cell you add, describing what that cell shows — it renders in the cell header and is what a reader skims instead of the code. A notebook holds at most 50 cells; past that the call fails, so start a new notebook rather than retrying.",
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies notebook behavior and failure handling for the MCP tool, potentially aiding documentation or tests.
